meaning: A list of numbers a model returns for a clip, placed so that clips with similar content get lists that sit close together.
Decoding a video and encoding it again, usually into a different codec or as separate clips.
NVIDIA's toolkit for curating physical AI training data as a pipeline of CPU and GPU stages on a cluster.
A framework that spreads Python jobs across the machines of a cluster.
Fixed circuits on a GPU that only compress and decompress video, separate from the tensor cores that run neural networks.
NVIDIA's name for the fixed-function circuit on a GPU that compresses video.
NVIDIA's name for the fixed-function circuit on a GPU that decompresses video.
The open video codec LeRobot writes by default.
The part of a training program that fetches samples from storage and assembles them into batches for the GPU.
One of the dataloader's parallel processes; each runs on CPU cores and, in LeRobot, also decodes video.
The PyTorch project's video decoder, which LeRobot runs on the CPU by default.
The unit EC2 counts processor capacity in; on x86 instances with two threads per core, one vCPU is one hardware thread.
One physical core presenting itself as two hardware threads so that it can interleave two programs.
Random changes applied to each image during training, such as shifts in brightness or framing.
A small imitation policy that predicts a chunk of future actions from camera images and joint angles.
Turning compressed video back into frames of pixels; it is repeated every time training reads a frame.
A video frame stored whole, which a decoder can decode with no other frame.
The spacing of keyframes in a video; a random read costs at most that many decoded frames.
A format for compressing video into a file and turning it back into frames.
A video codec, also called H.265, that LeRobot can record in place of AV1.
The part of a GPU that multiplies matrices for a neural network.
Choosing which recordings a model learns from, by dropping failed attempts, still clips and near copies.
Clustering clip embeddings and dropping clips that sit too close to another, so near-identical recordings do not outweigh the rest.
A clustering algorithm that groups vectors around a chosen number of centres.
A score for two vectors that is 1 when they point the same way.
One real processor core; with two threads per core, 24 vCPUs are 12 physical cores.
The share of time a GPU's video decoder was in use, reported by nvidia-smi separately from the compute part.
In nvidia-smi, the percentage of the sample period during which at least one kernel was executing on the GPU.
EC2 capacity that AWS may take back from a running job.
NVIDIA's programming layer for running code on its GPUs.
NVIDIA's way of dividing one GPU into isolated slices; on a split card nvidia-smi cannot report decoder or GPU utilisation.
LeRobot's mode that trains from a dataset without downloading it first; Hugging Face reports 2.1 to 2.5 times more samples per second from four workers.
In a LeRobot dataset, one control tick of one episode; in the curation run's design note, one entry of the recipe's input table.
The time the GPU takes for one training step on a batch; LeRobot's guide reports it as update_s beside the data-loading time dataloading_s.
